title: Taipei's All-Night Art Festival Returns on October 31
summaryZh: 台北白晝之夜10月31日登場，30多件裝置、50場演出。
summaryHi: ताइपे का रात भर चलने वाला कला उत्सव 31 अक्टूबर को 30+ इंस्टॉलेशन और 50 प्रस्तुतियों के साथ लौटेगा।
summaryEs: La Nuit Blanche de Taipéi vuelve el 31 de octubre con más de 30 instalaciones y 50 espectáculos.
summaryJa: 台北の「白夜祭」が10月31日に開催、30以上の作品と50の公演。
summaryKo: 타이베이 밤샘 예술축제가 10월 31일 30여 개 작품과 50개 공연으로 돌아온다.
summaryEn: Taipei's Nuit Blanche art night returns on October 31 with over 30 installations and 50 shows.
paragraphs: Taipei's Nuit Blanche festival will light up Taipei Expo Park on October 31, offering more than 30 art installations and 50 performances that run from evening until the early hours of the next morning, city officials announced on Friday.

The 11th edition, themed "Night Ka Shi", will spread large-scale installations, sound art and mixed performances across the park's Yuanshan and Xinsheng areas, as well as nearby streets around Minzu East Road and Qingguang Market.

The theme is inspired by nakasi, a form of live music from the Japanese colonial era in which performers wandered between streets, banquets and other gatherings, playing on the spot. Organisers hope to recreate that spontaneous spirit by inviting visitors to discover art as they stroll.

This year the festival is partnering for the first time with Centquatre-Paris, a public cultural centre, whose director Valérie Senghor is acting as guest curator. A French diplomat in Taipei said two French art groups had been invited to offer fresh perspectives on the city.
Nuit Blanche was launched in Paris in 2002 to make art more accessible and help residents see their cities differently. Taipei held its first edition in 2016.
Taipei will have a big night of art this month. The event is called Nuit Blanche. These are French words. They mean "white night".
The art night is on October 31. It starts in the evening and goes on until very early the next morning. People can walk around and see art for free.
There will be more than 30 art works and 50 shows. They will be in Taipei Expo Park and the streets and markets near it. Some art will use sound and music.
This year, a big art centre in Paris is helping Taipei. Its boss is helping to choose the art. Two groups of artists from France are coming too.
Nuit Blanche started in Paris in 2002. Now many cities have it. Taipei had its first one in 2016. This is its 11th year.
Taipei's all-night art festival, Nuit Blanche, will return on October 31 with more than 30 art installations and 50 performances, the city's Department of Cultural Affairs said on Friday.

The event will take place in Taipei Expo Park and the nearby Yuanshan park, and also in streets close to Minzu East Road and Qingguang Market. It will begin in the evening and continue until the early hours of November 1.

This year's theme is "Night Ka Shi". It comes from nakasi, an old style of live music from Japanese times. In nakasi, musicians moved from place to place, playing in streets and at parties. The organisers want visitors to enjoy art in the same way, walking from one show to the next.
For the first time, Taipei is working with Centquatre-Paris, a public arts centre in France. Its director, Valérie Senghor, is the guest curator. Two French art groups have also been invited.
Nuit Blanche began in Paris in 2002, and many cities now hold their own version. Taipei joined in 2016, so this will be its 11th festival.

Taipei's Nuit Blanche festival will light up Taipei Expo Park on October 31, offering more than 30 art installations and 50 performances that run from evening until the early hours of the next morning, city officials announced on Friday.

The 11th edition, themed "Night Ka Shi", will spread large-scale installations, sound art and mixed performances across the park's Yuanshan and Xinsheng areas, as well as nearby streets around Minzu East Road and Qingguang Market.

The theme is inspired by nakasi, a form of live music from the Japanese colonial era in which performers wandered between streets, banquets and other gatherings, playing on the spot. Organisers hope to recreate that spontaneous spirit by inviting visitors to discover art as they stroll.

This year the festival is partnering for the first time with Centquatre-Paris, a public cultural centre, whose director Valérie Senghor is acting as guest curator. A French diplomat in Taipei said two French art groups had been invited to offer fresh perspectives on the city.
Nuit Blanche was launched in Paris in 2002 to make art more accessible and help residents see their cities differently. Taipei held its first edition in 2016.

Taipei is preparing for its annual night of open-air art, with organisers promising more than 30 installations and 50 performances when Nuit Blanche takes over Taipei Expo Park on October 31 and runs into the small hours of November 1.

Now in its 11th year, the festival has adopted the theme "Night Ka Shi", a nod to nakasi, the roaming live music that flourished during the Japanese colonial period. Musicians would drift between streets and banquets, improvising as they went, and the organisers hope visitors will roam the venue in a similar fashion.

Works will be scattered across the Yuanshan and Xinsheng sections of the park, the Yuanshan Natural Landscape Park and the neighbourhood around Minzu East Road and Qingguang Market, blending sound art with large-scale installations and hybrid performances.

In a first for the event, Taipei has teamed up with Centquatre-Paris, whose director Valérie Senghor is serving as guest curator. French officials in Taipei said two invited French collectives would offer contrasting readings of the city's urban landscape.
The concept originated in Paris in 2002 as a way of democratising access to contemporary art, and it has since been adopted by cities worldwide. Taipei staged its inaugural edition in 2016.

Taipei's Nuit Blanche, the city's annual celebration of contemporary art after dark, will return on October 31, featuring more than 30 installations and 50 performances that will continue until the early hours of the following morning.

The eleventh edition has been conceived around the theme "Night Ka Shi", a reference to nakasi, an itinerant form of live music that emerged during the Japanese colonial era. Performers traditionally moved spontaneously between streets and banquets, and the curators intend to evoke that informal, mobile atmosphere by encouraging audiences to encounter art while wandering.

Installations and sound pieces will be distributed throughout Taipei Expo Park and the surrounding district near Minzu East Road and Qingguang Market, thereby integrating the festival into ordinary public spaces rather than confining it to galleries.

Notably, the event has forged its first partnership with Centquatre-Paris, whose director, Valérie Senghor, has been appointed guest curator. French representatives in Taipei suggested that the collaboration would foster cultural dialogue and stimulate further international cooperation in the arts.

Originating in Paris in 2002, Nuit Blanche was designed to make art more accessible and to prompt residents to perceive familiar surroundings in a new light. The model has since been replicated globally, with Taipei hosting its first edition in 2016.
